introduction: Simple Interest (SI) is the fixed interest earned/paid on the original principal only, unlike Compound Interest. SSC CGL tests basic SI/Amount calculation, finding rate/time/principal from given ratios, multiple-rate and multiple-part investment problems, and doubling/multiplying time problems.

concepts.explanation: SI = (P x R x T)/100, where P=Principal, R=rate% per annum, T=time in years. Amount = P + SI.
If SI is a given fraction of P (e.g. SI=1/4 of P), set numerator=SI-part, denominator=Principal-part directly for quick ratio solving.
If Amount becomes n times Principal in T years, then SI = (n-1) x 100% of P, giving direct rate-time relation.
If sum becomes k times in T years at SI, then SI%=100(k-1)%; for m times, time = T x (m-1)/(k-1).
When rate changes across different time slabs, calculate SI% slab-wise and sum: r1xT1 + r2xT2 + r3xT3 = total SI%.

concepts.concept: Sum divided into parts with equal/given interest
concepts.explanation: When a sum is split so that parts at different rates/times give equal or ratio interest, use inverse ratio of (rate x time) to find principal ratio.

concepts.concept: Difference of SI at two rates
concepts.explanation: Difference in SI on same P for same T at rates R1,R2 = P x T x (R1-R2)/100.

formulas: If sum becomes k times in T years: R = 100(k-1)/T
Time to become m times = T x (m-1)/(k-1), using known doubling/tripling time T
Difference of SI at R1% and R2% for same P,T = PxTx(R1-R2)/100
When P divided in parts with rates r1,r2...: equal-interest parts ratio = inverse of (rate x time) product

question_types.identification_method: Direct question giving any 3 of P, R, T, SI/Amount and asking the 4th.
question_types.when_to_use: Apply SI=PRT/100 directly; convert R to fraction for clean numbers.
question_types.shortcut: Use fraction form of rate (12.5%=1/8, 11.11%=1/9) instead of decimals.
common_mistakes: Not converting months into fraction of year for T

practice_questions.q: ₹500 invested at 10% p.a. for 2 years. Find SI.
SI on ₹12000 in 12 years is 120% of principal. Find rate.
Sum amounts to 5/4 of itself in 3 years. Find rate%.

question_types.identification_method: Different interest rates applied for different consecutive time periods.
question_types.when_to_use: Sum rate% x time% for each slab, equate total to given SI% or SI value.
step_by_step: List rate and duration for each slab
Compute r x t for each slab and sum
Equate to total SI and solve for P or unknown rate
question_types.shortcut: Treat as percentage of principal directly (100%=P) to avoid extra multiplication.
common_mistakes: Missing a slab's time or rate
Adding rates without multiplying by respective time

practice_questions.q: 5% for 3yrs, 8% for 2yrs, 10% beyond 5yrs; total SI=₹12,750 over 7yrs. Find sum.

question_types.identification_method: Sum doubles/triples/becomes n times in given years; asks time for another multiple.
question_types.when_to_use: Convert 'doubles' to 100% SI, then scale proportionally to new multiple.
step_by_step: Find SI% for the given multiple (k-1)x100%
Scale time proportionally for new multiple using same rate
question_types.shortcut: Double=100% in T years; triple=200%; n times=(n-1)x100% — scale time directly.
common_mistakes: Assuming linear multiple of years directly without adjusting for SI%

practice_questions.q: Sum doubles in 7 years. In how many years will it become 5 times?
Amount becomes 9 times in 20 years. When will it be 13 times?

question_types.identification_method: A sum split into 2-3 parts invested at different rates/times, with a condition on their interests (equal, ratio, or difference given).
question_types.when_to_use: Use inverse ratio of (rate x time) for principal ratio when interests are equal; otherwise set up direct equations.
step_by_step: Identify rate x time for each part
If interests equal, take principal ratio as inverse of rate x time
Apply given total sum to find each part
question_types.shortcut: Equal interest condition → Principal ratio = inverse of respective (RxT) products.
common_mistakes: Using direct ratio instead of inverse ratio for equal-interest condition

practice_questions.q: Vipul, Ashima, Priya invest total ₹21,000 at 3%,6%,5% resp., equal interest. Find Ashima's investment.
₹6000 split; SI on part1 at 10% = SI on part2 at 15%. Find interest on each part.

question_types.identification_method: Question asks present worth of a sum due after T years, or difference of SI between two rates/banks.
question_types.when_to_use: Present worth = future sum x 100/(100+RT); Difference of SI = PxTx(R1-R2)/100.
step_by_step: Apply present worth formula or difference formula directly
question_types.shortcut: Present worth is simply reverse of amount formula.
common_mistakes: Using SI formula instead of present worth formula

practice_questions.q: Present worth of ₹1,100 due in 2 years at 5% SI.
SI difference from two banks on ₹8000 in 3 years is ₹800. Find R1-R2.

identification_tricks: Only P,R,T,SI/Amount mentioned directly — Basic SI type.
Different rates for different year-slabs — Multiple Rate Slab type.
'Doubles/triples/becomes n times' wording — Multiplying Time type.
Sum split into parts with equal/ratio interest condition — Parts Division type.
'Due after T years' or 'two banks difference' — Present Worth/Difference type.
solving_approach: Step 1: List all known values: P, R, T, SI, Amount.
Step 2: Convert wordy relations (fraction of sum, multiple of sum) into percentage form directly.
Step 3: For multi-rate/multi-part problems, break into slabs/parts and handle separately.
Step 4: Use 100%=Principal trick to avoid repeated multiplication.
Step 5: Cross-check answer using Amount = Principal + SI relation.
shortcuts: Convert rate% to standard fractions (12.5%=1/8, 16.66%=1/6, 11.11%=1/9, 6.25%=1/16) for fast calculation.
Doubling time formula: 100/R years to double at simple interest.
Equal SI parts ratio = inverse of (rate x time) product — no need for full equation setup.
Set Principal=100% for ratio-based SI questions to skip variables.
common_mistakes: Confusing SI with Amount in given data.
Forgetting to convert months to years fraction in T.
Using direct ratio instead of inverse ratio for equal-interest split problems.
Not adjusting rate x time properly in multi-slab rate questions.
pyq_patterns: SSC CGL frequently tests sum-doubles-then-multiplies-time chain questions.
Multi-rate slab and multi-part investment problems with equal/ratio interest are very common.
Present worth and SI difference between two schemes/banks appear in Tier-1 regularly.
Word problems involving fraction of sum as SI or amount are a recurring pattern.
quick_revision: Equal SI parts ratio = inverse of RxT
exam_tips: Convert all rates to fraction form for speed.
Always express relations as percentage of principal to avoid variable-heavy equations.
For multi-slab rate problems, tabulate rate and time per slab before summing.
Double-check whether question asks for SI or Amount before finalizing answer.

one_page_formula_sheet.doubling: R=100(k-1)/T for k times in T years
